correctness.rationale: Reintegrated the depth mean after v=q exp(-u) to M_q(t)=e/t integral_0^t[q exp(-u)exp(-q exp(-u))]du. The response f_q(u) has derivative f(q exp(-u)-1). For q<=1 it decreases strictly; for q>1, g=t f(t)-integral f increases until log q, decreases thereafter, starts at zero and tends to -(1-e^-q), so exactly one positive global maximum. At the stationary point y=q exp(-t) in (0,1), the equation t y=1-e^(y-q) gives partial_t G=t y(y-1)<0 and partial_q G=[1-(1+q-y)e^-(q-y)]/q>0, proving strict q-monotonicity by the implicit-function theorem. Taylor/analytic IFT at (q,t)=(1,0) gives the 3/2 coefficient; t*y=1+O(e^-q) yields t=log q+log t+O(e^-q), hence double-log limit. Independent symbolic Taylor and direct quadrature/bracket checks agree, but no finite data prove the asymptotics.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge PASS for the all-q unique optical-depth optimizer, strict monotonicity and two sharp asymptotics, NOT for the Steele physiological curve or the integrated-column production formula. Steele (1962) introduced response; Bannister (1974) derives related depth-integrated exponential production equations, explicitly acknowledged as prior. Walsby (1997) supplies numerical integration in time/depth under more complex circumstances. Idso–Foster (1975) and Murphy (1962) are plausible prior sources; accessible abstracts alone cannot exclude a stronger optimizing statement. The Oxford attempt for Idso–Foster returned vpn_disconnected; no access bypass attempted. Generic unimodal running-mean optimization is a residual possible dominating principle; full claim coverage not established by inspected text.
